video_title: Is OKC-Spurs the BEST Rivalry in NBA?!?

quotes.speaker: DeMarcus Cousins
quotes.summary_phrase: DeMarcus Cousins on the need for more competitive NBA rivalries
quotes.excerpt: I'm tired of all the friendly shit. Enough is enough, let's get back to competitive basketball.

text_blocks.speaker: DeMarcus Cousins
text_blocks.text: I like it. I think it's good for the game, I think it's good for the sport. I'm tired of all the friendly shit. Enough is enough, let's get back to competitive basketball. Let's get back to not liking each other. And I think a lot of that kind of starts with Victor Wembanyama. He comes from another country, but this dude plays with an edge and he's continuing to show us that he's far from a pushover. He's far from a pushover, however you want to put it.

text_blocks.speaker: Chandler Parsons
text_blocks.text: This isn't just physical either. This is two great teams, two teams that are contenders, two teams that just flat out don't like each other. I wish they would just come out and say that so we don't have to keep saying that without fully knowing.

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: Chandler Parsons on the need for an OKC enforcer
quotes.excerpt: I just want to know who's going to be the enforcer on OKC when teams do rough them up.

text_blocks.speaker: Chandler Parsons
text_blocks.text: I just want to know who's going to be the enforcer on OKC when teams do rough them up. Is it going to be the other Jalen Williams? Is it going to be Jaylin Williams?

text_blocks.speaker: DeMarcus Cousins
text_blocks.text: It's going to be Jaylin Williams. What do you mean?

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: Chandler Parsons on Victor Wembanyama's offensive consistency
quotes.excerpt: Sometimes he floats, sometimes he settles. I don't really like it when he takes a bunch of outside jumpers.
quotes.quote: Sometimes he floats, sometimes he settles. I don't really like it when he takes a bunch of outside jumpers and doesn't get to the free throw line. So at least when the bucket wasn't falling last night, he was getting to the free throw line. But it is weird at his size and his ability and the way he moves, he can't get an offensive rebound, tip dunk. He can't get to his little baby hook. I still want to see him work on that when he gets a mismatch in the post because when you're talking about Victor Wembanyama, he doesn't have to get to a mismatch. Whoever is guarding him, it's already a mismatch. So he doesn't need to be waiting for everything. And I think like this when I watch Jayson Tatum and Luka Doncic play, these guys are so gifted, but sometimes they let the defense off the hook and they don't get to the right spots and they don't get downhill. And I think Victor Wembanyama is a product of that where he just settles too much.

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Lou Williams on the Spurs' lack of offensive sets for Wembanyama
quotes.excerpt: I don't see any dedicated sets that San Antonio is running to get Victor Wembanyama the basketball.
quotes.quote: I'm still going to split it still from where I was last year. Half of it is going to be coaching, half of it is going to be Victor Wembanyama needing to be more aggressive. Maybe I missed it, but I don't see any dedicated sets that San Antonio is running to get Victor Wembanyama the basketball. I don't see that. I see him maybe eating off the land or them running plays for other guys. But run something where there's a back screen for a lob or some. Run something where there's a quick duck in for him to catch the ball two feet from the rim. Something of that sort to get him easy baskets, especially when you look at a game last night. He doesn't get his first field goal until the third quarter. If you want to win games, you know this guy has to be an intricate part of your offense. So halfway through the first quarter, whether it's the first play of the game or anything, the press has to stop. Everything has to stop until we get this guy going. Once we get this guy going, then we can start worrying about everybody else.

quotes.speaker: DeMarcus Cousins
quotes.summary_phrase: DeMarcus Cousins on simplifying Wembanyama's offensive game
quotes.excerpt: I would just like to see him simplify his game. It's a lot of plays where he's working so hard.
quotes.quote: I would just like to see him simplify his game. It's a lot of plays where he's working so hard to even get a shot attempt off. And sometimes I think he forgets that he's the tallest guy on the floor. His game can be so simple sometimes where he can just catch at the free throw line, turn around, and shoot it. No tween-tweens, no crossover dribbles, no ducking the show, literally turn around and shoot over the top of the defender. The same thing goes for each block. Turn around, shoot over the defender. I've said this before, I'm going to say it again, I don't know what's going on behind closed doors with the Spurs. I don't know what's being taught to him behind closed doors. I don't even know if it's even being taught or worked on. But for him to continue to get better, and he does need to get better, he's far from a finished product. LaMarcus Aldridge is one of the best turnaround shooting big men this game has ever seen. Why isn't he on staff and working with this kid every single day? Tim Duncan with the bank shot from anywhere on the floor, anywhere in the paint. Why is it this being added to Victor Wembanyama's game?
